key_findings.title: Transformer‑based models dominate performance
key_findings.summary: Architectures such as DPT and MiDaS‑v3 set new state‑of‑the‑art records on KITTI and NYU‑Depth V2 by leveraging global context modeling.

key_findings.title: Self‑supervised learning expands data applicability
key_findings.summary: Methods that exploit video streams or stereo pairs eliminate the need for dense ground‑truth depth, enabling training on massive uncurated datasets.

key_findings.title: Multi‑task training improves robustness
key_findings.summary: Joint prediction of depth, semantics, and surface normals yields higher accuracy and better generalisation across domains.

key_findings.title: Domain‑generalisation techniques mitigate deployment gaps
key_findings.summary: Style randomisation, feature‑level alignment and test‑time adaptation are critical for maintaining performance on unseen environments.

key_findings.title: Real‑time, edge‑friendly depth estimation remains under‑explored
key_findings.summary: Current literature is benchmark‑centric and lacks models that balance high accuracy with low latency suitable for edge devices.

synthesis: Between 2023 and 2025, monocular depth estimation has been reshaped by transformer‑based backbones, which consistently outperform convolutional rivals on legacy benchmarks such as KITTI and NYU‑Depth V2. Parallel advances in self‑supervised learning permit scaling to video and stereo data, removing the bottleneck of dense ground‑truth annotations and fostering broader in‑the‑wild applicability. Researchers increasingly adopt multi‑task frameworks that co‑predict depth, semantics, and surface normals, a strategy that enhances robustness and cross‑domain generalisation. To address domain shift, techniques like style randomisation, feature alignment, and test‑time adaptation have become standard, yet evaluations remain confined to a limited set of datasets, overlooking newer large‑scale suites (e.g., TartanAir, Waymo Open). Crucially, the field still lacks real‑time, edge‑optimized solutions; most high‑performing models demand substantial compute, hindering deployment on mobile or embedded platforms. Consequently, future work should prioritize lightweight transformer designs, benchmark diversification, and systematic assessment of domain‑generalisation under realistic runtime constraints.
